# Results — Study 768 (Charm-Decay) on real SPY daily tape

*Generated by [`examples/verify.py`](../examples/verify.py). The charm (delta-decay)
dealer-flow story: in the last week before monthly options expiration the deltas of the
dealer book bleed with time, and the popular claim is that the re-hedging drives SPY **up
into OpEx** and lets it **fade after**. Tested on SPY daily bars 1993–2026 as a directional
window/event study, with a calendar-randomisation placebo. As-of **2026-07-10**; the content
fingerprint pins the exact tape.*

## Data stamp

| Ticker | Window | n | Fingerprint |
|---|---|---|---|
| SPY (auto-adjusted, total-return proxy) | 1993-01-29 → 2026-07-10 | 8,418 days | `a7ff45641491` |

- Monthly OpEx dates defined (1993–2026): **408**
- Pre-OpEx (charm) window days in tape: **2,005** (5 sessions ending on each OpEx)
- Post-OpEx window days in tape: **2,005** (5 sessions after each OpEx)
- Execution: position set by the exchange calendar (known before the month begins) — no
  price look-ahead; entered at the prior close so the first window day's full return is earned.

## Leg 1 — Pre-OpEx charm-window drift

The headline claim: SPY drifts **up** in the five sessions ending on OpEx. It does not — the
window return is a hair *below* baseline, and utterly insignificant.

| Window | Mean | Baseline | Difference | HAC *t* | n |
|---|--:|--:|--:|--:|--:|
| **Pre-OpEx (charm week)** | +4.54 bps | +4.85 bps | **−0.32 bps** | **−0.13** | 2,005 |
| Post-OpEx (give-back week) | +3.48 bps | +5.18 bps | −1.70 bps | −0.76 | 2,005 |

The pre-OpEx window is not a rally; the post-OpEx window is weakly (insignificantly)
soft. Neither clears |t| = 2.

## Leg 2 — The "rally then fade" asymmetry

The single number the narrative predicts to be large and positive — mean pre-OpEx minus
mean post-OpEx return:

| Contrast | Pre mean | Post mean | Difference | HAC *t* |
|---|--:|--:|--:|--:|
| Pre − Post | +4.54 bps | +3.48 bps | **+1.05 bps** | **+0.31** |

A +1 bps/day tilt in the storybook direction, drowned in noise (t = +0.31). There is no
tradable rally-then-fade asymmetry.

## Leg 3 — Quarterly (triple-witching) restriction

If the charm flow is concentrated where the option book is largest (quarterly expiries), the
pre-OpEx drift should be strongest there. It is not — it is, if anything, more negative:

| Sub-sample | Pre-OpEx diff | HAC *t* | n |
|---|--:|--:|--:|
| All months | −0.32 bps | −0.13 | 2,005 |
| Quarterly only (Mar/Jun/Sep/Dec) | −1.06 bps | −0.23 | 670 |

## Leg 4 — Placebo / calendar-randomisation (the decisive test)

Slide the OpEx anchor by every fake offset of ±5…±30 trading days and re-measure the
pre-window HAC *t*. This builds a null distribution of *t*-stats from arbitrary calendar
anchors that are **not** OpEx. The real anchor should sit in the tail if charm is real.

| Quantity | Value |
|---|--:|
| Real-anchor pre-window *t* | **−0.13** |
| Placebo anchors (n) | 52 |
| Placebo mean \|*t*\| | 1.08 |
| Placebo max \|*t*\| | 3.68 |
| Empirical two-sided p-value | **0.94** |

The real OpEx anchor is *less* remarkable than **94%** of random calendar anchors — several
arbitrary "fake OpEx" dates produce a bigger drift *t* than the real one (max |*t*| = 3.68).
The window is indistinguishable from picking a random week of the month. This is the
falsification: the OpEx anchor carries no special directional information.

*(Machinery check: on a synthetic tape with a **planted** +8 bps pre-window drift, the same
placebo returns true-*t* = +3.59 against placebo mean |*t*| = 0.90, p = 0.019 — the harness
isolates the true anchor when there is one to isolate.)*

## Structural break — pre/post-2012 (the charm-narrative era)

Charm/vanna flow narratives went mainstream after ~2012 (weekly options, then the 0DTE
explosion). If the drift were a modern microstructure artefact it should be *stronger* in
the later sub-period. It flips sign to *negative* instead:

| Period | Pre-OpEx diff | HAC *t* | n |
|---|--:|--:|--:|
| Pre-2012 (1993–2011) | +1.20 bps | +0.35 | 1,135 |
| Post-2012 (2012–2026) | −2.25 bps | −0.67 | 870 |

Neither is significant, and the modern era — precisely when the story got popular — drifts
the *wrong* way.

## Tradability — the charm overlay

| Strategy | n (active) | Mean | Sharpe | CAGR | HAC *t* |
|---|--:|--:|--:|--:|--:|
| Long pre-OpEx window only | 1,992 | +4.57 bps | +0.62 | +10.2%/yr | +1.87 |
| Long pre / short post ("rally then fade") | 3,983 | +0.53 bps | +0.07 | **−0.4%/yr** | +0.31 |
| Buy-and-hold SPY | 8,417 | +4.78 bps | +0.65 | +10.9%/yr | — |

The long-only overlay earns the **same Sharpe per dollar of exposure as buy-and-hold**
(0.62 vs 0.65) — its +1.87 HAC *t* is market beta collected on ~24% of days, not charm
alpha. The full rally-then-fade long/short returns **less than cash** (−0.4%/yr, Sharpe
0.07) before a single basis point of cost or borrow. A 0.5 bp one-way cost, paid entering
and exiting once a month, leaves nothing.

## Verdict

- **Signal — NONE.** The pre-OpEx charm window drift is −0.32 bps vs baseline (HAC
  *t* = −0.13); the rally-then-fade asymmetry is +1.05 bps (*t* = +0.31); the quarterly
  restriction is null; the modern era drifts the wrong way. Nothing clears |t| = 2.
- **Tradability — MIRAGE.** The long overlay is buy-and-hold beta; the long/short trade
  earns less than cash gross, and any cost erases it.
- **Charm rally? — BUSTED.** The calendar-randomisation placebo puts the real OpEx anchor
  at the 94th percentile of *arbitrary* anchors — the OpEx week is not special. The charm
  Greek is real physics; the tradable directional drift it is claimed to produce is not in
  the SPY tape.
